summary: Bounded independent exact-source semantic review found no substantive defect in the six frozen production modules. Their actual graph incidences, ordered witness counts, internally selected minimum, and local swap/fiber statements support the stated limited conclusions. This is not a completed cleaning argument, a total new-witness upper bound, a main upper spanner theorem, or a whole-paper/source-arithmetic audit.

scope.mode: Read all 775 lines of the six new production modules, inspect relevant unchanged definitions and proof dependencies, verify frozen hashes and supplied local gate logs, and write this report only.
scope.original_source_arithmetic_concern: Unresolved and outside this review. Nothing here certifies a new source defect or a counterexample to the original theorem.

gate_evidence.verification_method: Read recorded pass markers and all log contents; no compiler or official kernel replay was rerun by this reviewer. Source hashes were checked independently against the frozen manifest.
gate_evidence.audit_implementation_inspected: The paper-local verification/AxiomAudit.lean selects every declaration by its defining imported module, including private/generated declarations, collects transitive axioms, rejects anything outside the three allowed axioms, and rejects an empty audit. The aggregate log reports 898 declarations.
gate_evidence.qualification: Recorded local gates are not independently rerun exact-commit CI certification.

findings: starCollision is the actual directed count n*(n-1) on the filtered leaf-neighbor set. orderedStarSurplus sums truncated natural-number surplus over ordered distinct selected centers; absent fibers contribute zero.

The two directional collision sums agree by swapping summation indices. Enlarging the second center domain to all host vertices is a valid nonnegative finite-sum bound. The factor 2 is explicit, and badStarPairCount remains an ordered pair count.

The mate-free budget is supplied by the existing exact ordered-pair/common-neighbor double count, with ell*(ell-1) formed in natural numbers before casting. Empty and singleton leaf sets introduce no invalid real subtraction.

selected_fiber_surplus_le uses the actual quotientCrossEdges subset of the undirected host edgeFinset, mapped through the actual fullStarLabel. The existing selected_edge_fiber_card applies with real bipartiteness, C subset B, packing, and distinct labels. It returns the sum of the two crossing-leaf cardinalities.
limits: orderedStarSurplus is an ordered sum, not the full undirected quotient-loss total. Residual fibers, internal loss allocation, and a bound on the bad score are not supplied.

findings: The counted mates are literal original-host common neighbors. The mate-set convention agrees exactly with the existing Unmated predicate, rather than substituting an unrelated numerical incidence hypothesis.
The injection to a mate union is through starHitCenters_card, which uses genuine branch disjointness from the packing and the explicit Disjoint A C premise.

The quantitative bound explicitly requires that every vertex of the fixed center-plus-leaf branch is small in the host graph and that this branch has ell leaves. The resulting branch cardinality is exactly ell+1.

The nonmated-center bridge handles cross-branch pairs using absence from the actual filtered set and handles same-branch pairs using both original-host MateFreeOn premises. Neither old branch premise was dropped.
limits: This is a bound for mated centers, not the outstanding unmated bad-incidence bound.

findings: unmatedBadCenters retains both actual IsBadStarPair and absence from the real matedStarCenters set. Each leaf class additionally requires actual adjacency to that center.

Every bad pair has exactly one crossing leaf in the fixed star because its real filtered cardinality is one. Existence proves coverage of the union; uniqueness makes classes for distinct leaves disjoint.
The cardinality conclusion is therefore an exact finite sum over the old leaf set, not an assumed incidence budget or a union bound with silently duplicated centers.
limits: No numerical per-leaf upper bound is asserted.

findings: The representation stores two ordered, center-oriented leaf edges ((b,u),(c,v)) selected from a true bad pair. The crossing leaves are unique, so canonical choice does not introduce multiplicity or remove possible witnesses.
Projection to the two centers makes badForestWitness injective, and the cardinality equals the literal ordered badStarPairCount exactly.

mem_badForestPairs exposes center membership, old leaf ownership, and both real cross edges. With IsStarPacking, the represented center-leaf edges are also host edges. Their endpoints also meet the literal starForestGraph adjacency definition.
Reversing a witness retains membership. badForestOutgoing_card is a genuine bijection with actual bad neighboring centers through a specified owned leaf.
loss_le_gain is the valid finite-set difference inequality derived from the score comparison; it does not itself assume or prove a global upper bound.
limits: Raw witness definitions do not require a packing. Their host-edge interpretation is explicitly established when a packing is supplied. Global forest acyclicity needs the existing disjoint center/leaf-domain hypotheses and is not newly asserted here. The count is ordered, not a count of unordered pairs of forest edges.

findings: Removing u from its old owner destroys every outgoing witness at (b,u). Reversal supplies an equally large second set of destroyed witnesses. The two sets are disjoint because overlap would force a bad pair with identical centers.
Thus each bad neighboring center through the removed leaf contributes two distinct ordered witnesses, including both directions; the factor 2 is present throughout the lower bound.
The swap is the literal global leaf-label transposition. Packing disjointness proves distinct owners have distinct leaves and that u is absent from its old owner afterward.

The existence theorem calls exists_minimum_bad_star_family internally. That unchanged dependency uses Nat.find on attainable natural scores with the input family as a witness, then Nat.find_min prime for comparison. It does not take an optimization oracle as an existence-theorem hypothesis.

The swapped candidate is proved admissible using real cross edges and bipartiteness; leaf cardinalities, covered-leaf union, and original-host branch mate-freeness are preserved. For every actual unmated bad neighbor, a real reverse crossing leaf is extracted and the original-host union-mate-free bridge supplies the needed premise.
The final inequality lower-bounds new ordered edge-pair witnesses by twice the size of the actual unmated bad-leaf incidence class.
limits: This is a lower bound on created witnesses, not an upper bound or a cleaning result. The existence statements preserve a real minimizing family and admissible swaps; they do not provide an algorithmic runtime claim.

findings: The crossing updates use the real swapped leaf set: erase the old leaf, then insert the new leaf exactly when it is adjacent to the fixed center. Unchanged third-star crossings require both d not equal b and d not equal c.

The new-bad/no-inserted-adjacency classification retains both exclusions. It uses the unchanged reverse crossing count and failure of old badness to show the removed old leaf was adjacent; the old forward count was exactly two.
The produced w lies in (L b).erase u and both u and w are adjacent to the actual third center d in G. The right-side statement correctly swaps the roles and both exclusions.

The finite charge uses the supplied D throughout, followed by an honest union bound and containment in actual commonNeighbors u w. Erasure guarantees w differs from u, allowing the original-host MateFreeOn bound. No extra distinctness or incidence oracle is missing.

A selected bad pair has an actual adjacency in fullStarContraction and exactly two undirected host edges in its quotientCrossEdges fiber. The natural surplus is exactly one. The swapped-family specialization first proves a valid packing from actual cross edges.
The admissibility bundle preserves both old branchwise and old-union mate-free premises in G and obtains branch disjointness from bipartiteness and C subset B.
limits: The exceptional class covers newly bad center pairs with no inserted-leaf adjacency only. It is not a classification or upper bound for every newly created ordered forest-edge witness.

integration_obligations_not_defects: A newly created ordered forest-edge witness can occur while its center pair remains bad before and after the swap, because the unique leaf witness changes. A future total gain upper bound must count such persistent-bad-center cases as well as newly bad center pairs.

Any future total new-witness upper bound must also account for inserted-leaf-adjacent cases, both exchanged stars, the pair between the exchanged centers, reversal multiplicities, and overlaps between charging classes.
Converting the local selected-selected fiber estimates into the full simple-quotient loss requires the remaining residual-fiber allocation and global cleaning argument.
No quantitative total new-witness upper bound, cleaning theorem, density increment, completed main upper spanner theorem, or new source defect follows from this reviewed checkpoint.
